Visible

/VIZ-uh-bul/ — stress on VIZ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Visible describes something that can be seen.

From the ridge, three states are visible on a clear day.

Worked Example

The theater's new stage lighting made the actor's facial expressions clearly visible even from the back row.

Vis (see, from Latin) + -ible (can be done) = can be seen. The design ensured that subtle facial expressions were fully seen from distant seats — visible captures precisely what the lighting achieved: the ability to perceive the actor's face clearly throughout the theater.

How Visible Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

perceptible

perceptible: able to be noticed by the senses

apparent

apparent: plain and obvious at a glance

discernible

discernible: just barely able to be made out

Antonyms

invisible

invisible: impossible to see at all

imperceptible

imperceptible: too slight for the senses to notice

How Strong Is It? — detectable → discernible → noticeable → visible

detectable vs. visible

detectable vs. visible: A detectable trace of smoke needs instruments or very sharp senses to find, but a visible plume can simply be seen.

discernible vs. visible

discernible vs. visible: A discernible outline can just barely be made out if you squint, while something visible stands plainly before your eyes.

noticeable vs. visible

noticeable vs. visible: A noticeable smudge catches your eye once you look at the window, but a fully visible stain is right there for anyone to see.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vis-

Root — vis-: to see (from Latin videre, whose past participle is visus) (Latin)

Suffix — -ible

Suffix — -ible: able to be; capable of being (Latin (-ibilis))

Put it together

Put it together: vis- ('see') + -ible ('able to be') = able to be seen. It is the same vis- hiding in vision, visual, and television — literally 'seeing at a distance.'

Use the root in a new word: visualize

Use the root in a new word: visualize: Before the race, she closed her eyes to visualize every turn of the track.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Visible is the precise word when something can be perceived by sight, often emphasizing that it was previously hidden or hard to detect. Use it when visibility itself — the ability to see something — is the key point.
